Women's Disorders

Seeking Heirs

When a woman has her period, there may be pain or flow, and afterward blood and qi contend with one another, so that conception cannot occur — whether the discharge is purple or black. Whether one seeks a son first or seeks a child after, the primary approach is always to regulate the menstrual cycle. Each time menstruation occurs, one must regulate it.

To harmonize the menstrual channels, when husband and wife unite, the spirit must be calm and the seed chamber properly prepared; desire must follow its proper course, with little distraction, and the channels must be regulated each month.

Although yin deficiency is present, one must not overly suppress it; the mind must not be disturbed. The best strategy is to follow the proper path and minimize excessive desire.

One must preserve the spirit and nourish it in due time. Even when the husband stirs arousal, one must not let the fire blaze up; the vital essence must be conserved and not squandered. It is appropriate to supplement, and the man must have abundant essence with minimal desire and a calm mind.

This is how conception is achieved. For the man, Warm the Kidneys Pill (溫腎丸) and similar remedies nourish and strengthen yang and replenish essence. These should be taken in due time to supplement. Use them in combination once a year with calming and gentle preparations.

Therefore, taking Warm the Kidneys Pill continuously will warm the kidneys, clear and supply the palace, and strengthen the weak. For men, use formulas to consolidate the pulse and strengthen yang.

For general use: Yuwang Key Formula, Yingying Formula, Heshi Formula, Shigong Formula, and for women, similar formulas are appropriate.

Methods for Examining Women (相女法)

Women who have no children — in many cases this is due to insufficiency of essence and the need to regulate and nourish the blood. It is appropriate to use [various formulas] to nourish the blood, regulate menstruation, warm the uterus, and supplement yang. When a woman conceives but cannot carry the child to term due to constitutional weakness, [appropriate medicines] should be administered.

[Various medicinal formulas and herbs are indicated for conditions such as:] Driving out dampness, nourishing the blood, warming the uterus, dispelling stagnation. Herbs such as Pinellia (半夏), Ligusticum (川芎), Talcum (滑石), Phellodendron (黃苓), and others are used accordingly.

Conditions of phlegm, food stagnation, and obstruction of the uterus causing irregular menstruation and poor constitution in women are also addressed.

Pulse Methods (脈法)

When the pulse at the chi (尺) position is slippery and rolling like beads, this indicates the essence and spirit are present. When the pulse is deep and faint or weak without strength, this is a sign of deficiency. If the right chi pulse is deep and the left is slightly slippery, this tends toward excessive desires and poor temperament.

When the palace [uterine] pulse is full and the blood is plentiful and the physique is good, fertility is favorable. When the pulse is thin, irregular, and the physical appearance and character are poor, conception is difficult.

On Avoiding Inauspicious Times for Yin-Yang Union (Sexual Intercourse)

If one chooses the proper time to unite, there is nothing that will not come to fruition. From the moment a person begins life, it is blood [that is fundamental].

The sea [of vitality] begins to grow: on the first, second, and third days, the essence and spirit are said to be flourishing. The gate [of vitality] is open, and this governs the timing.

[Regarding conception:] The jade [essence] is thin; one must face forward on the first day — this is called the flourishing of the divine spirit. Those who do not seek a child should still follow the method of union with their spouse.

After the passing [of menstruation], on the first day, the essence and vitality are renewed. If one unites during the four seasons — spring, the jiǎ and yǐ days, the second month, through summer and the bǐng days — one may conceive.

For wind, rain, meetings under rainbows, fog, thunder, great cold, the bǐng-dīng days, great heat, lightning, and at new and full moon — these are all times to avoid union.

One must not engage in union inside Buddhist temples or shrines; if one does not follow proper method and timing, blessings and virtue will not accumulate.

If one follows the proper methods and the way of the household, virtue and blessings will flourish. If one does not follow proper guidance, calamities will follow, as sure as a needle's prick.

Nurturing the Fetus in the Tenth Month

During a woman's pregnancy, at the first and third months the foot lesser yin meridian nourishes; at the sixth month the yang brightness meridian nourishes; at the fourth and second months the foot lesser yin meridian nourishes; at the eighth month the hand greater yang meridian nourishes; these concern the fetal water and yang; at the ninth month various meridians nourish; therefore, in each month the yin nourishes through the greater yang meridian; those who begin nourishment at the fourth month use the greater yang foot and eighth month meridian nourishes.

For thirty days, the nourishing of the child activates the pulse; the child nourishes the hand and foot lesser yin and greater yang meridians; at ten months the child's heart and vital essence are cultivated.

Milk, essence, and vital energy flow through the meridians to nourish the fetus; the mother's blood and fine red blood circulate.

First Month

At the first month, the father's essence and the mother's menstrual regulation converge; the meridians open to nourish the fetus. The fetus is like a sphere of yellow color, like a single precious bead, quiet and still, gradually forming within the fluid sac.

The outer layer forms a wrapping of yellow and mixed colors; inside, the embryo gradually consolidates, round as a ball, resting quietly, the fluid sac enclosing it.

It then resembles a small pellet, like a pill, round; after seven days it transforms further, consolidating gradually.

During this time one should not overexert, should avoid emotional disturbance, and must refrain from excessive eating and drinking, so that the child may grow healthily through the year.

Tenth Month:
The Foot Taiyang Bladder meridian nourishes the fetus; it receives the five organs' functions and brings birth.

Pulse During Pregnancy:
When the middle pulse waving is very strong it is called "turbulent water." If the Shaoyin pulse beats strongly in the hand and the Yang pulse is separate, this is called the Yin-chi moving pulse.

When pressing the pulse and it is not slippery or rapid, but when pressing hard it disperses — yet the rapid quality does not disappear — this indicates the fifth month of pregnancy. If all three positions of the pulse feel heavy under pressure and float under the hand, this indicates the eighth month, third position, and the pulse is heavy — because it is a Yang pulse, therefore the fetus is heavy.

[Further passages discuss pulse distinctions for pregnancy:] If the pulse of the lesser yin and greater yang are distinct and the chi (cubit) pulse moves, the woman is pregnant. If it is a full, rounded pulse in the hand indicating a son; if the pulse characteristics differ, other determinations are made. By the third month the yang pulse confirms the pregnancy.

When all five viscera are fully prepared and await their time, birth occurs naturally. The governing official oversees the six seasonal periods of life.

The Kidney meridian pulse at its node nourishes the fetus; beginning at the third month it receives the mineral essence, enabling the five organs to form, and activating movement in both the left and right hands.

The pulse that is sunken, upright, firm and forceful — when pressed it has no bowstring-like tautness; a tight pulse indicates pregnancy. A sunken and thin pulse indicates death. In the eighth month of pregnancy the pulse is six or seven [beats per breath].

Double Fetus / Special Fetal Presentations:
The way of Qian (Heaven) produces males; the way of Kun (Earth) produces females. The husband's Qian and Kun, yin and yang in nature are the essence. This text discusses the foundational principles of yin-yang theory as applied to human reproduction and fetal development in traditional Chinese/Korean medicine. The following is a faithful rendering of its content:

The path of the Dao: the ceremonial distinctions between male and female, yin and yang, are the foundation of the household. The father's essence (jing) and the mother's blood, stirred by the physician's understanding of sensation and response, unite to form the body. The essence-qi resides on the right; named substances complete it. The right is called "radiance" (ying). The left essence divides and is absorbed. If male, then on the left the essential qi meets, and the two branches of the womb-element are felt; the fetal origin thus arises. This is how blood and form become the yang. Women and the coloring of form — or at times when the essence is insufficient — the yin-yang sequence proceeds and the day of formation arrives.

When the essence-qi does not harmonize and the division of absorption differs, if the fetus belongs to the left with the same essence-qi having the same sensation and the right is firm, the male divides and absorbs from the left essence. The right is called "radiance." Named substances complete the essence; it resides on the right, where blood transforms into the yin fetal body and nourishes it. Blood then forms into yang as the next step.

Three selections: if the person is old, even though a fetus forms, a male may not result. The fetal attributes belong to the left; with the same essence-qi and same sensation, the fetus forms. The husband's role: the yin within the yang — thus the fetus may have twins; opposing the fetus in yin, if sensation is present, then the yin divides and the qi of the male form is lost. Form and coloring, or when essence is insufficient — the yin-yang sequence then proceeds.

Sheep Kidney
Harmonizes and treats postpartum deficiency and weakness, lack of strength, and general debility. Take one pair of sheep kidneys, roast and slice finely, make into a thin gruel with five spices; good for bone and joint pain, or cook in a pot as a good food. Also finely slice pig kidney and make into thin gruel to eat; for difficult labor, dress with oil and steam.

Pig Kidney
Adjust with water, divide portions, and immediately [give to the patient]. Cook eight chestnuts with the bone, make into otter-food [gruel] and eat to relieve difficult labor.

Musk
Easily treats and collects [the fetus], and also induces labor and causes descent of the fetus. Take one qian dissolved in water and drink to induce delivery.

Elm Bark (White Bark)
Easily induces delivery, greatly raises and expels the fetus, causing immediate death and expulsion. In cases where a person is ill and wishes to remove the fetus, take the bark powder and boil the white bark into a decoction. Take one qian twice daily.

Sweet Bamboo Root
Easily treats restless fetal movement. Boil sweet bamboo root into a decoction and drink. [Also applicable with] Korean bamboo.

Xuegen (Madder Root): Two treatments for pregnant women. Removes and dislodges the fetus. For cases where the woman desires to abort, treats abdominal pain that is unbearable. A wondrous remedy — do not take it lightly.

Qu Mai (Fringed Pink/Dianthus): Take internally to break up and expel the fetus. Stir-fry. Treats difficult labor and death of the fetus. Treats difficult delivery.

Che Qian Zi (Plantain Seeds): Treats difficult labor and failure to deliver. The juice does not come out. This is the method.

Shui Yin (Mercury): Take two liang, look into the middle of it, and the child will come out. For retained placenta that will not descend, with the fetus dead in the womb and large masses forming.

Da Huang (Rhubarb Root): Treats difficult labor, transverse presentation, failure to collect, and cutting off of the umbilical cord. Treats difficult labor and recurrent difficult deliveries.

Acupuncture and Moxibustion Methods:
For male patients: apply moxibustion at Gall Bladder point, five cones of moxa. There is no need for needling — the Korean tradition says it is sufficient. For filling and blocking the conception vessel, apply moxa at the Gate of Life point, left and right sides. Also apply moxa at the Zi Hu (Child's Door) point. Moxibustion at the Gate of the Origin point, right side, three days of moxibustion, thirty cones, to the count of two. Or needle the border of the Gate of Origin. Seven cones, or needle — immediately induces labor.

For difficult labor: Yin Jiao, Shi Men, expels dead fetus. Take Da Chong, Fu He, Gu, San Yin Jiao, Qiu Xu, San Lian, Jia Yi — from the Jia Yi Jing.

For retained lochia (after delivery, the malignant blood not yet expelled): half a sheng, cook together into a paste, form pills the size of wutong seeds, take with water.

Dongui Bogam, Miscellaneous Diseases, Volume 10

[Section on difficult labor and retained placenta, acupuncture methods:]

At the time of labor, to relieve difficulty: needle the point Juque (巨闕) six fen deep, retaining the needle for seven breaths, to obtain qi. This helps the birth proceed correctly and regulates the person.

For the method of using needles on the mother's eye point: insert the needle into the center of the palm to reach Juque, retaining for seven breaths to obtain qi. If there are needle marks toward the point of birth, the child's bones will descend, and the spirit-qi will immediately cause the ghost-influences to cease.

For cases where the placenta is retained after delivery, or for difficult labor: take the points on the right leg, named in the Bogam — needle to the small alarm point, take the upper needle, cutting off the worm influence, for the spirit-shen.

For three instances of non-delivery, immediately after delivery, for swelling, for three li [points], take water and various medicines combined.

For retained placenta after birth, for swelling below, three li points.

[Supplementary instructions:] These are the acupoints: press and record; after [needling], by oneself there will be movement of the pulse responding under the fingers. Place transversely, calm the heart, keep straight — all instruct the woman afterward to take [the treatment]. Seven moxa cones at both ends to exhaustion.

Fix, mark, hands and feet, to measure by listening — heart, one, illuminating the sea, Shenjue (神闕), Yuanyin point — take the placenta-clothing after birth, three measures.
These points: press and record afterward, self-movement of the pulse responds under the fingers transversely — calm the heart, keep straight — all instruct the woman afterward to take [the treatment], reclining, mouth open.
